joint_spanning_method: OLS with Newey-West (21 lags) standard errors
construction: 12-month sign trend blended at equal risk weight with roll-yield (basis) momentum; per-market volatility sizing; 7% portfolio volatility target; monthly rebalance with a 25% no-trade band; integer contracts.
comment: Joint spanning regression on the five-rule published family: alpha 4.64% annualized, HAC t 6.04, R-squared 0.735. Only mop_tsmom carries a significant loading (0.509, t 15.16); the other four loadings are indistinguishable from zero. The incumbent is a half-weight, risk-controlled MOP plus something the family does not span.

role: primary comparator: canonical published trend rule
source: Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen (2012), JFE 104(2): 228-250, eq. (1) and (5)
construction: 12-month sign, no skip month; 40% per-instrument ex-ante volatility budget (60-day centre of mass, lagged one session); 1/S_t weights; no portfolio volatility control and no leverage cap.
primary_comparator_rationale: mop_tsmom is the fairest primary comparator because it is the published rule the incumbent's trend sleeve is a variant of, run cold on the identical 59-market panel through the identical execution seam and cost model (benchmark_seam_check.csv: maximum absolute daily net-return deviation 0.0), so the only differences left are the ones under review.
comment: HONEST READ: MOP earns MORE raw CAGR than the incumbent (13.84% against 13.19%), and it takes 1.55x the volatility and 1.79x the peak-to-trough loss to get it. On risk-adjusted terms the ordering reverses. mop_tsmom is the fairest primary comparator because it is the published rule the incumbent's trend sleeve is a variant of, run cold on the identical 59-market panel through the identical execution seam and cost model (benchmark_seam_check.csv: maximum absolute daily net-return deviation 0.0), so the only differences left are the ones under review.

source: Hurst, Ooi & Pedersen (2017), JPM 44(1): 15-29, incl. footnote 5
construction: equal-weight sign blend over 1/3/12-month horizons; per-market inverse-volatility sizing; portfolio scaled to a 10% ex-ante volatility budget on a 36-month equally weighted covariance.
comment: The strongest published rule on Sharpe after the incumbent, and the only other one whose drawdown stays inside 16%. Its spanning loading is not significant once mop_tsmom is in the regression, so the two trend rules are largely the same bet.

source: zero-timing control implied by Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen (2012) sec. 4.1
construction: X = +1 in every market with MOP inverse-volatility sizing at a 40% per-instrument budget. A passive long futures panel, not a market portfolio and not a CAPM beta reference.
comment: The zero-timing control. Correlation with the incumbent is 0.18, so this is not a factor the incumbent is disguising: it is the passive alternative, and it loses 42% peak-to-trough to earn less.

source: matched-volatility protocol after Harvey et al. (2018)
construction: long_only_equal_risk with the per-instrument budget bisected until realised 1990-2014 volatility equals the incumbent's. The constant is an EX-POST full-sample calibration and is not causal.
comment: Equalises the risk axis so CAGR is comparable directly: at the incumbent's 7.7% volatility the passive book returns 6.50% against 13.19%, with a drawdown more than twice as deep. The matching constant is fitted ex post on the full sample and is therefore favourable to the control.

role: published volatility-managed trend rule: strongest independent comparator
source: Barroso & Santa-Clara (2015), JFE 116(1): 111-120, applied to MOP TSMOM
construction: MOP TSMOM scaled by the inverse of its own trailing realised variance (126-session window, causal), targeting a constant volatility. An independent published rule on an independent published signal.

role: published trend rule, matched leverage constraint
source: Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen (2012) under this repository's 5x gross cap
construction: mop_tsmom with the incumbent's gross-notional ceiling imposed, so the comparison is not flattered by the incumbent's own leverage constraint.

source: Baltas & Kosowski (2013/2020), Demystifying Time-Series Momentum Strategies
construction: Position sized by the t-statistic of the trailing trend regression rather than its sign, so conviction scales with statistical strength.

source: Baz et al. (2015), Dissecting Investment Strategies in the Cross Section
construction: MACD / EWMAC exponential crossover cascade, the standard practitioner trend construction, volatility-normalised per market.

source: zero-timing control, equal dollar notional per market
construction: X = +1 with equal notional rather than equal risk, so commodity volatility dominates. The weakest reference and the least informative.

role: OVERLAY ON THE STRATEGY ITSELF - not an independent benchmark
source: Barroso & Santa-Clara (2015) volatility management applied to this strategy
construction: The incumbent's own decisions re-scaled by trailing realised variance. Beating it is not evidence of an edge: it is the same strategy at a different risk level, and it scores within 0.002 Sharpe of the incumbent.

role: OVERLAY ON THE STRATEGY ITSELF - not an independent benchmark
construction: Volatility-managed overlay on the incumbent's own returns, with the scaling constant estimated on an expanding window (causal).

role: OVERLAY ON THE STRATEGY ITSELF - not independent, and not causal
source: Moreira & Muir (2017) with a FULL-SAMPLE scaling constant
construction: As above but the constant is fitted on the whole sample, so it uses information unavailable at the time. Reported only to bound the overlay family; it is not an achievable result.
